cands.name: Renee A. Price
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina House District 50 (Orange and Caswell counties) since January 2023. Earlier she served on the Orange County Board of Commissioners from 2012, including as chair. Her career includes urban and environmental planning, housing, grant writing and a forestry program for Black landowners.

endorsements.text: For 2026, Ballotpedia lists endorsements from Sierra Club North Carolina, the Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party, the Center for Freethought Equality, the 92% Club and Jess's Progressive Picks.
Her campaign site lists endorsements from Carrboro Mayor Barbara Foushee, Hillsborough Mayor Mark Bell, several NC House members, Sen. Natalie Murdock and Orange County commissioners.

cands.gaps: We could not find when Price moved to North Carolina or where she was raised; she says only that she was born in Rochester, NY. We found no bills she sponsored (the sponsored-legislation list on her page was empty). We found no documented actions of hers on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership limits, growth, immigration, policing, guns or school choice. We found no stated positions from her on those topics either, apart from reproductive rights. We found no documented stance on data centers or development, no controversies and no foreign ties. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, so her stated positions come mainly from a 2022 survey and her campaign site.

local.label: Roots 40: She was born in Rochester, NY, and says she worked in New York, North Carolina and Alabama; she was elected an Orange County commissioner in 2012, so she has lived in North Carolina as an adult for at least about 14 years, but the date she moved here is not stated.

qual.background: Member of the NC House since 2023 (appropriations-related committee assignments). Orange County Commissioner from 2012, re-elected twice, serving as chair. Master's in regional planning; past roles include housing director, assistant project manager for an environmental impact office, grant writer for a law firm, forestry program director and government relations manager.
qual.why: She has prior and current legislative service and more than a decade of local elected office. Her planning, housing and policy career is also relevant to writing law and budgets.
